title: Scattering several updates into a scalar fails to compile, and so does `grad` of the matching `gather`
description: Scattering several updates into a scalar with `lax.scatter_add` fails to compile with an internal error of XLA,
and so does `jax.grad` of the matching `lax.gather`, whose transpose rule is that scatter.
The gather itself works, and so does a scatter of a single update,
which is what `x.at[()].add(u)` emits, with indices of shape `(0,)`.
expected: An operand of rank 0 has no axis to index, so its index vectors are empty.
Indices of shape `(3, 0)` are three such index vectors:
`lax.gather` reads the scalar three times, and `lax.scatter_add` should add three updates to it.
So the gradient of the sum of the gathered values is 3, as forward mode computes.
reproducer: # Three empty index vectors: a scalar has no axis to index.
f = lambda x: lax.gather(x, indices, gather_dnums, slice_sizes=())
# The transpose rule of gather is this scatter_add, which adds three updates to the scalar.
cause: In XLA. `_scatter_lower` emits the scatter as it is, and it is valid StableHLO.
The pass `ScatterSimplifier` of XLA rewrites a scatter into a scalar to one call of the update computation,
as if there were a single update, and the call does not type-check with three updates.
On an operand of higher rank, the same scatter compiles but returns a wrong result:
the algebraic simplifier of XLA applies the update computation elementwise, as if update `k` went to position `k`.
fix: In XLA. Until then, JAX can combine the updates over the scatter axes before it lowers,
so that one update remains: `scatter_add` sums them, and `scatter_mul`, `scatter_min` and `scatter_max` use their own operation.
lean: The model computes the scatter: `Jax.Lax.scatterAdd` adds every update to the scalar.
`Jax.Lax.gatherTranspose_correct` proves the transpose rule of `gather` correct for these arguments,
so the rule is right and the compiler fails.
`scripts/shapes.py` found the failure when it compared the positions that the model and JAX write to.
